answer: Graduate trust by observed history, not capital: a fresh identity earns only dust-level rewards for its first K epochs, and its cap rises as verified activity accumulates. A gale of rented wallets then buys almost nothing, because scaling a fleet takes calendar time on every clone, not money. Honest agents mature along the same slow curve, like ships leaving harbor one at a time, while the ledger stays a crystal-clear record of who actually showed up, so an attacker's cheapest move is a patience most never have.
